All work is complete and every gate is green. Here is the summary.

## Result
- Goal/task: G-20260804T095105533205Z-224ce02d / **T-20260804T095105535495Z-22a51036** — "Reach the carry from CI and record the decision"
- Role: Implementer (default, ADR 0008)
- Status: **ready** (implementation complete, all local evidence green; loop owns commit/PR/merge)

## What changed or decided
Wired the dormant base-sync carry (`guardian_comment_carried`, ADR 0018) into CI so it actually applies, and recorded the decision.

- **Both workflows, 4 judging invocations** now pass `--base-sync-carry` and `--default-branch "$DEFAULT_BRANCH"`, with `DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}` in each step's `env:`:
  - `shiki-cca-completion.yml` — `cca` job: the `guardian_approval_signal.py` signal and the `shiki guardian status` blockers render; `mergegate` job: `mergegate_check.py`.
  - `shiki-mergegate.yml` — the metadata `mergegate_check.py` (its run body stays expression-free; `DEFAULT_BRANCH` flows through `env:`).
  - Reused each job's existing base fetch — **no second fetch, no `--depth`**.
- **`validate_shiki.py`**: added both flags to the `shiki-mergegate.yml` entry and a **new top-level entry for `shiki-cca-completion.yml`**. I guarded all four invocations (not just the two the scope named) because acceptance check #4 requires validate_shiki to fail when *any* of the four loses either flag — documented in-code.
- **CCA prompt** (`.github/prompts/cca-completion-check.md` + inline in `shiki-cca-completion.yml`): CCA-08 reads `guardian_comment_carried` as a recorded authority and must not re-run the base-sync proof.
- **ADR 0018** written: Context (head-bound approval × strict protection; measured 4 extra approvals across 5 Contract PRs on 2026-08-01), Decision (guardian_comment only, tree reproduction, ordered fail-closed conditions, default off, code-pinned), Alternatives (one-PR serialisation; `merge -s ours`/evil-merge defeat diff/patch equality; 4-of-8 real syncs overlap `.shiki/tasks/*.json` kills disjointness), accepted residual, Consequences.
- **`guardian-policy.md`**: new carry section; every prior needle verified intact.
- **Tests**: new `tests/test_workflow_invocation_carry.py` (enumerates all invocations, both flags each; `DEFAULT_BRANCH` env; expression-free; no `--depth`/second fetch; 4×2 per-invocation-per-flag validate failures). Updated `tests/test_workflow_invocation.py` (`--base-sync-carry`→`_STORE_TRUE`, `--default-branch`→`_FLAG_VALUES`, staged `shiki-cca-completion.yml`). Added a carry block to `test_shiki_control_plane.sh`.

## Checklist status
- Skill Gate: `tdd` (tests written/red-green-verified), `code-review` (self-reviewed; scope-bounded) — satisfied
- TDD: negative controls proved validate fails per flag before wiring; all tests green after
- CCA/MergeGate: not run locally (GitHub authority)

## Evidence
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` → **919 passed**
- `bash scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh` → passed; **all 34 `test_shiki_*.sh`** pass (incl. governance-evidence, guardian-policy, workflow-lint, shellcheck --strict)
- `python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target .` → passed
- `git status` confirms **only the 9 locked files** changed (the untracked `.shiki/tasks|locks/*.json` are loop-owned, untouched)

## Next action
- Hand back to the Shiki loop to commit, push, open the PR (MergeGate body), and merge. Risk is **high**, so MergeGate/Guardian approval applies on the PR — and this task is exactly the one that makes an already-approved high-risk PR carry its approval across a proven base sync.

One design note worth surfacing for review: the scope named two CCA invocations for the validate_shiki entry, but acceptance check #4 requires validate_shiki to fail for **all four** named invocations (including the guardian-status render). I guarded all four — a superset of the scope's naming — to satisfy check #4 literally; this is strictly safer (prevents silent flag removal on the render too) and still "covers both judging invocations."
